sources.entry: Restreamer - Access H.264 real-time video streaming on your website without a streaming provider. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: Restreamer is a self-hosted, Docker-based live streaming server that receives streams, republishes them to websites (HLS) and platforms like YouTube-Live, Twitch, and Vimeo, and includes a web UI and REST API.
summary.what_it_does: Restreamer runs as a Docker container and accepts live video inputs, then serves them over HTTP/S (HLS), RTMP/S, and SRT. It can re-stream those feeds to external platforms such as YouTube-Live, Twitch, Vimeo, Twitter, and software like Wowza Media Server. It includes a built-in VideoJS player and a configurable publication website for embedding streams on your own site. The web interface offers a setup wizard, and a REST API with Swagger documentation is provided. The README also mentions viewer and bandwidth monitoring with limiting, optional Prometheus metrics, server and process logging, and automatic Let's Encrypt HTTPS. Hardware acceleration is listed for Raspberry Pi (MMAL/OMX), Nvidia CUDA, and Intel VAAPI.
use_cases: Live stream video on your own website without a streaming provider
Re-stream one live feed to YouTube, Twitch, and Vimeo at once
Run a self-hosted RTMP or SRT ingest server
Serve live video as HLS to web viewers
Encode live video on a Raspberry Pi or GPU machine
Monitor viewers and bandwidth for live streams
how_to_run: Use datarhei/restreamer:rpi-latest on ARMv7/ARM64 Raspberry Pi (adds --privileged)
Use datarhei/restreamer:cuda-latest with --runtime=nvidia --privileged for Nvidia CUDA
Use datarhei/restreamer:vaapi-latest with -v /dev/dri:/dev/dri --privileged for Intel VAAPI
Build a custom bundle by cloning datarhei/ffmpeg, datarhei/core, and datarhei/restreamer-ui and building each with docker build
notable: Ready-made Docker images for AMD64, ARM, Raspberry Pi, Nvidia CUDA, and Intel VAAPI hardware
Built-in VideoJS player and embeddable publication website
Multi-platform restreaming to YouTube-Live, Twitch, Vimeo and others
Claims GDPR compliance without third-party providers and no audience data saved
caveats: Hardware acceleration and local devices need --privileged or specific runtime flags
External access may require port forwarding on your router
Commercial support is offered separately by the vendor (contact support@datarhei.com)
